### 3.5 Diagnostic registry

Level decides delivery. **Error**: the chart or a series cannot be drawn; the chart shows its error state. **Warning**: something is not drawn as given; the reader sees the note in F12. **Hint**: advice for the author. Errors and warnings print once per code per page in every build; hints print in development builds only. `strict: true` throws on errors and warnings found while validating a create, `update` or `append` call, synchronously from that call. A diagnostic that can only arise later (a contrast check after the page's CSS changes, a custom formatter that throws when a table page is built, a label that stops fitting after a resize) is reported when it is found and is never thrown. Every diagnostic names the chart; those about data name the field and the first row indexes in the caller's own data.

item.text:
I found **two blockers**. Valid calendar dates can hang tick generation, and a narrow numeric range can produce a reversed domain that excludes every input value. All 92 existing tests passed.

### Findings

1. **B — Year ticks can hang layout.** `timeTickCandidates` failed to return within a one-second timeout for a UTC year axis from `0000-01-01` to `0002-01-01`. I reproduced the same timeout for years `+200000` through `+200010`. The year loop eventually asks `utcFields` for an unrepresentable date. It returns `NaN`, so `w > wallHi` can never terminate the loop. Bound iteration by the endpoint year and stop on non-finite boundaries. Apply the same guard to the month loop. [scale/time.ts:229](/home/canarit/projects/axylo/packages/axylo/src/scale/time.ts:229)

2. **B — Narrow ranges around a large value produce reversed bounds.** For `min=100000000`, `max=100000000.01`, and `includeZero=false`, I observed the automatic domain `[100000000.08, 99999999.93]`. Tick generation on the original interval offered only `100000000`. The relative tolerance moves the starting index by dozens of ticks, but the correction loop repairs at most four. Start from the unshifted quotient and compare adjacent representable multiples against the endpoint. Generate tests from a base value plus a small width. The current property explicitly filters this case out. [scale/nice.ts:55](/home/canarit/projects/axylo/packages/axylo/src/scale/nice.ts:55) · [scale/nice.ts:65](/home/canarit/projects/axylo/packages/axylo/src/scale/nice.ts:65) · [linear.test.ts:103](/home/canarit/projects/axylo/packages/axylo/test/scale/linear.test.ts:103)

3. **M — Finite numeric extremes produce unusable domains and pixels.** For `[-1e308, 1e308]`, I observed an automatic domain of `[NaN, NaN]` and no tick candidates. With that explicit domain and pixel range `[0,100]`, `map(0)` returned `0` and `invert(50)` returned `Infinity`. The midpoint should map to `50` and invert to `0`. At the other extreme, `[5e-324, 1e-323]` also produced `[NaN, NaN]`. Compute spans and interpolation in scaled coordinates when subtraction overflows. Use the finite input bounds when a nice step underflows or outward rounding has no finite result. [scale/domain.ts:38](/home/canarit/projects/axylo/packages/axylo/src/scale/domain.ts:38) · [scale/linear.ts:25](/home/canarit/projects/axylo/packages/axylo/src/scale/linear.ts:25)

4. **M — Subhourly ticks repeat labels across a DST fold.** For `America/Los_Angeles` on `2026-11-01`, from `07:45Z` through `09:45Z`, the 15-minute candidate labeled both `08:15Z` and `09:15Z` as `1:15 AM`. The code checks only adjacent labels. Detect repeated local clock readings across the entire candidate and add the zone or numeric offset to both occurrences. The time property currently accepts any nonempty label. [scale/time.ts:318](/home/canarit/projects/axylo/packages/axylo/src/scale/time.ts:318) · [time.test.ts:199](/home/canarit/projects/axylo/packages/axylo/test/scale/time.test.ts:199)

5. **M — A midnight gap can move a daily tick past the start of its day.** In `America/Toronto` on `1919-03-31`, `Intl` showed that clocks jumped from the previous evening to `00:30` at `04:30Z`. The daily candidate placed March 31 at `05:00Z`, already `01:00` local. Compatible disambiguation shifts the requested midnight by the whole gap. For calendar boundaries, locate the first instant of the target local date. Keep compatible disambiguation for callers converting an arbitrary wall time. [scale/time.ts:152](/home/canarit/projects/axylo/packages/axylo/src/scale/time.ts:152)

6. **M — F7 full-scale endpoints are lost during subsequent rounding.** A constant percent series at `100` with `includeZero=false` produced `[90,110]`. A constant ratio at `1` produced `[0.9,1.1]`. With percent data `[-1000,75]`, the upper bound became `500`. In all three cases the maximum qualifies for full scale. Preserve the selected upper endpoint through constant expansion and round only the unconstrained end. [scale/domain.ts:72](/home/canarit/projects/axylo/packages/axylo/src/scale/domain.ts:72)

7. **M — F6 readouts discard significant fractional digits.** I observed `0.000123456` → `0.000123`, `1.23456789e-7` → `0`, and `123456.75` → `123,457`. I read F6’s “full integer part and up to six significant fraction digits” as preserving `123,456.75` and allowing leading fractional zeroes before the six significant digits. Implement that rule explicitly. The integer-preservation property derives its expectation from the formatted output itself. A formatter returning `"0"` for every generated input would pass that property. Derive expected digits from the input and include magnitudes below `1e-6`. [format/number.ts:38](/home/canarit/projects/axylo/packages/axylo/src/format/number.ts:38) · [number.test.ts:83](/home/canarit/projects/axylo/packages/axylo/test/format/number.test.ts:83)

8. **M — Percent conversion changes rounding, and ratio conversion can throw during layout.** For declared percent `10.00005` with author option `maximumFractionDigits: 4`, I observed `10%`. Formatting the exact decimal fraction `0.1000005` with the same `Intl` percent options produced `10.0001%`. Dividing by 100 first loses the decimal tie. Separately, default ratio ticks on `[0,1e307]` threw `RangeError: maximumSignificantDigits value is out of range` after display scaling overflowed. Shift decimal exponents without an intermediate binary rescale, including when computing tick precision. [format/number.ts:45](/home/canarit/projects/axylo/packages/axylo/src/format/number.ts:45) · [format/number.ts:89](/home/canarit/projects/axylo/packages/axylo/src/format/number.ts:89) · [format/number.ts:143](/home/canarit/projects/axylo/packages/axylo/src/format/number.ts:143)

9. **M — Distinct numeric ticks can all display as zero.** On `[0,1e-21]`, the densest candidate contained 11 distinct positions. Every label was `0.00000000000000000000`. When the step exceeds the formatter’s fixed-decimal precision, switch to localized scientific notation with enough digits to distinguish neighbors. Test label uniqueness using the production labeler. [format/number.ts:147](/home/canarit/projects/axylo/packages/axylo/src/format/number.ts:147)

10. **M — Readouts can lose the required zone or unit.** In Los Angeles, the author options `{hour:'numeric', minute:'2-digit'}` rendered both `2026-11-01T08:30Z` and `09:30Z` as `1:30 AM`. F4 requires the zone in the heading. For numeric readouts, `unit:'ms'` with `format: v => v.toFixed(1)` rendered `3` as `3.0`. Conversely, a default percent readout with `unit:'%'` rendered `12` as `12% %`. Compose the required metadata once, accounting for symbols already supplied by `Intl` or the author. [format/time.ts:87](/home/canarit/projects/axylo/packages/axylo/src/format/time.ts:87) · [format/number.ts:99](/home/canarit/projects/axylo/packages/axylo/src/format/number.ts:99)

11. **M — A singleton author domain is silently widened.** With `authorDomain:[5,5]` and `includeZero:false`, I observed `[4.4,5.6]`. F7 gives author bounds precedence, and the continuous scale already maps a singleton to the pixel midpoint. Preserve `[5,5]` on a line. Apply the F1 widening rule when a bar or area requires zero. [scale/domain.ts:52](/home/canarit/projects/axylo/packages/axylo/src/scale/domain.ts:52)

12. **M — Category x formatters are ignored, including their AX160 fallback path.** With category `direct` and `format: v => v.toUpperCase()`, `x(0)` returned `direct`. Replacing the callback with one that throws still returned `direct` and produced no error callback. Invoke the formatter with the category name, fall back to the original name on failure, and report the field through the existing AX160 callback. [format/index.ts:82](/home/canarit/projects/axylo/packages/axylo/src/format/index.ts:82)

13. **M — Calendar readouts lose the era.** The distinct UTC dates `0000-01-01` and `0001-01-01` both rendered as `Jan 1, 1` in `en-US`. The former is 1 BC. Include a localized era for BCE values and wherever year labels would otherwise collide. [format/time.ts:45](/home/canarit/projects/axylo/packages/axylo/src/format/time.ts:45) · [scale/time.ts:282](/home/canarit/projects/axylo/packages/axylo/src/scale/time.ts:282)

14. **M — Category tick generation allocates hundreds of thousands of objects per layout.** For 100,000 distinct category names, I counted **534 candidate arrays and 265,909 tick objects**. The first set bypasses the 1,000-tick limit, and the loop visits every stride through `n`. Cache the full set when layout needs every category, jump directly between useful strides, and materialize thinned candidates on demand. Preserve unordered-category visibility and hidden-label reporting. [scale/band.ts:53](/home/canarit/projects/axylo/packages/axylo/src/scale/band.ts:53)

15. **m — Scale and format import each other’s private implementation.** A Node import trace showed `scale/time.ts` loading `format/intl.ts` and `format/time.ts` loading `scale/zone.ts`. This couples both modules even when a caller imports just one entry point. Put shared temporal and `Intl` primitives behind a neutral internal interface, or inject the needed functions at composition. [scale/time.ts:12](/home/canarit/projects/axylo/packages/axylo/src/scale/time.ts:12) · [format/time.ts:9](/home/canarit/projects/axylo/packages/axylo/src/format/time.ts:9)

### Verification

`npm run typecheck` exited 0. I ran the scoped Vitest suite with the thread pool, native config loading, and both caches disabled to keep the review read-only. The counterexamples above came from separate Node probes against the source modules.

```text
Test Files  8 passed (8)
     Tests  92 passed (92)
  Start at  02:09:26
  Duration  1.20s (tests 82%, transform 11%, import 6%, worker 1%)
```

No files changed. No public or core contract change is needed. Browser rendering, zoom integration, and chart-level delivery of diagnostic codes were outside this module review.

### Areas checked and found sound

- **F1 and ordinary domains** — Positive and all-negative bars included zero. Author bounds excluding zero set the AX110 widening flag. Empty data returned `[0,1]`.
- **Zone conversion** — Direct wall-to-instant probes identified the Lord Howe half-hour fold, Kwajalein’s 1969 repeated hours, Kathmandu’s quarter-hour gap, and Apia’s skipped day.
- **Modern calendar boundaries** — The scoped tests passed for leap day, month ends, year changes, and calendar-date invariance across viewer zones.
- **Ordinary numeric behavior** — Decimal ticks on `[0.3,0.7]` matched the decimal literals. Default `en-US` readouts rendered `-0`, `NaN`, and positive infinity as `0`, `NaN`, and `∞`.
- **Band geometry and input isolation** — Forward and reversed band-center inversion passed. Both module entry points loaded in Node without a DOM, and inspection found no writes to caller-owned inputs.
